disc is palindromic, so disc(x)/x^4 = Q(u) with u = x + 1/x and Q(u) = u^4 - 6u^3 + 7u^2 + 6u - 31
PROOF (integers + IVT): Q(-2) > 0 > Q(-1), so Q has a real root in (-2,-1) subset [-2,2], i.e. disc vanishes at a point of |x| = 1

gates.note: a grid minimum was reported as if it were the true minimum; the zero was always there and the sampling stepped over it

gates.claim: at the base point x = 1 the roots ARE well separated (|disc| = 23, min separation 1.35) -- the collision is a property of the arc, not of the 5_2 point

verdict.outcome: REFUTED. The discriminant of the GGM deformed 5_2 curve VANISHES on the transport arc |x| = 1, at theta = 137.9206708879635 deg, where two of the three y-branches collide exactly. min |disc| = 0, not 0.348.
verdict.proof: disc is palindromic, so disc(x)/x^4 = Q(x + 1/x) with Q(u) = u^4-6u^3+7u^2+6u-31. Points of |x|=1 correspond to real u in [-2,2]. Q(-2) = +49 and Q(-1) = -23, both exact integers, so IVT gives a root in (-2,-1). No numerics are used in the existence argument.
verdict.what_it_breaks: (1) qou-trns sub-gap 1's step 2, 'the branches never collide on the arc', which the k=0 pinning argument rests on; (2) the envelope theorem's IFT hypothesis, false as stated; (3) any downstream use of 'min |disc| = 0.348'.
verdict.where_0.348_came_from: a grid minimum from an ~N=360 scan of [0,pi]. The dip is narrow (|disc'| ~ 87), so the recorded value is about 87*pi/(2N). Refining to N=20000 gives 0.0068.
verdict.likely_repair_NOT_done_here: Sum_j V_j is SYMMETRIC in the roots, and symmetric functions stay analytic across a branch point even though individual branches do not. So working with the symmetric combination, or deforming the path off |x|=1 around x_0, should recover the transport. Neither is written; neither is assumed here.
verdict.not_refuted: the sum rule itself. This probe says nothing against it.
